question: Give an example of choosing not to escalate a conflict and resolving it informally instead.

raiseTranscript.text: I had a disagreement with another new engineer on how to implement a small feature. Instead of going to our manager, I suggested we grab coffee and walk through both approaches.
We realized the difference was minor and picked one together. I learned to check assumptions early.

raiseNotes: Q: Give an example of choosing not to escalate a conflict and resolving it informally instead.
Role: New grad on first team, peer disagreement on implementation details
Situation: Two approaches to a small feature, risk of manager involvement
Action: Suggested informal coffee chat instead of escalation
Outcome: Aligned on one approach, shipped on time
Quote: 'I learned to check assumptions early.'
Follow-up: How did you know when to stop the conversation? 'Once we both saw the tradeoffs were small, we decided quickly.'
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for junior. Competency is Conflict Resolution. Story shows candidate chose direct peer conversation over manager escalation on a feature disagreement. Quote captures the learning: 'I learned to check assumptions early.' This meets junior expectations for ownership of own work and coachability. The outcome stayed local and did not require formal process. Biggest strength is recognizing when informal resolution was sufficient without over-involving others.

lowerTranscript.text: There was tension with a teammate about task ownership. I mentioned it to my manager in our 1:1 so it wouldn't get worse.
Did you try talking to them first?
Not really, I was worried it would make things awkward.

lowerNotes: Q: Give an example of choosing not to escalate a conflict and resolving it informally instead.

Situation: Avoided direct conversation, went to manager
Action: Raised in 1:1 without attempting informal fix
Outcome: Manager mediated, felt awkward afterward
Quote: 'I was worried it would make things awkward.'
Follow-up: What did the manager do? 'They set up a meeting for us.'
junior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for junior. Competency is Conflict Resolution. Candidate defaulted to escalation without attempting an informal conversation first. Quote reveals avoidance: 'I was worried it would make things awkward.' This shows limited ownership of resolving their own interpersonal issues. Junior level expects basic attempts at direct resolution before involving authority. Biggest gap is lack of evidence they tried the informal path the question asked for.

raiseTranscript.text: Two teams disagreed on API contract changes that affected both roadmaps. I set up a quick sync with the other tech lead instead of raising it in the planning meeting.
How did you keep it from escalating?
We walked through the impact numbers and found a smaller change that worked for both. No formal escalation needed.

raiseNotes: Q: Give an example of choosing not to escalate a conflict and resolving it informally instead.

Situation: Two teams' roadmaps at risk over contract changes
Action: Private sync with other tech lead, shared impact data
Outcome: Smaller compromise reached, both teams unblocked
Quote: 'We walked through the impact numbers and found a smaller change that worked for both.'
Follow-up: What if the other lead had pushed back? 'I would have asked for their constraints first before proposing options.'
senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for senior. Competency is Conflict Resolution. Candidate used direct cross-team conversation to resolve an API conflict that could have reached planning forums. Quote shows data-driven informal approach: 'We walked through the impact numbers.' This demonstrates influence without authority and cross-team impact expected at senior level. Outcome stayed informal and produced a workable compromise. Biggest strength is protecting team velocity by avoiding formal escalation channels.

lowerTranscript.text: A neighboring team kept changing requirements on a shared service. I documented everything and brought it up in the monthly steering meeting.
Why not reach out directly first?
I wanted a record in case it became a bigger issue.

lowerNotes: Q: Give an example of choosing not to escalate a conflict and resolving it informally instead.

Situation: Neighboring team changing scope repeatedly
Action: Documented and raised in steering meeting
Outcome: Formal discussion occurred, relationship stayed strained
Quote: 'I wanted a record in case it became a bigger issue.'
Follow-up: Did the direct conversation happen later? 'Eventually, after the meeting.'
senior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for senior. Competency is Conflict Resolution. Candidate chose formal documentation and steering meeting over an initial direct conversation with the other team. This approach created unnecessary process overhead. Biggest gap is missing evidence of trying to resolve cross-team tension directly before escalating.

raiseTranscript.text: Two reports on my team had ongoing friction over code review speed. I pulled them into a short offline conversation rather than using the performance process.
I asked each what the other needed to succeed and had them agree on a simple checklist. No formal write-up.

raiseNotes: Q: Give an example of choosing not to escalate a conflict and resolving it informally instead.
Role: Engineering manager, direct report friction
Situation: Two engineers clashing on review turnaround
Action: Facilitated private conversation, focused on mutual needs
Outcome: Checklist agreed, reviews improved without HR involvement
Quote: 'I asked each what the other needed to succeed.'
Follow-up: How did you follow up? 'Checked in two weeks later; both confirmed it was working.'
manager.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for manager. Competency is Conflict Resolution. Candidate handled direct-report friction through an informal facilitated conversation instead of performance documentation. Quote illustrates people-development focus: 'I asked each what the other needed to succeed.' Manager level expects creating leverage by resolving issues at the lowest level. Outcome avoided formal process while improving team dynamics. Biggest strength is modeling informal resolution and protecting team psychological safety.

lowerTranscript.text: I had two engineers arguing about ownership. I sent them both an email laying out expectations and copied my manager.
Why email instead of talking to them?
I wanted everything in writing for accountability.

lowerNotes: Q: Give an example of choosing not to escalate a conflict and resolving it informally instead.
Role: Manager, ownership dispute between reports
Situation: Engineers arguing about feature ownership
Action: Sent expectations email and copied skip-level
Outcome: Tension continued, team felt micromanaged
Quote: 'I wanted everything in writing for accountability.'
Follow-up: Did you meet with them together? 'Not at first.'
manager.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for manager. Competency is Conflict Resolution. Candidate defaulted to written communication and skip-level copy instead of direct informal conversation with the two engineers. Quote reveals preference for documentation over dialogue: 'I wanted everything in writing.' Manager level requires handling underperformance or friction through direct coaching first. This created unnecessary formality and reduced trust. Biggest gap is failing to use informal resolution to develop the team.

raiseTranscript.text: Sales and Engineering were at odds over a major customer commitment that would require re-prioritizing the roadmap. I met with the VP Sales privately before the exec sync.
We aligned on a phased delivery plan that protected engineering capacity. No org-level escalation occurred.

raiseNotes: Q: Give an example of choosing not to escalate a conflict and resolving it informally instead.

Situation: High-stakes customer promise threatening org priorities
Action: Private alignment meeting with VP Sales before exec forum
Outcome: Phased plan agreed, protected team capacity without formal dispute
Quote: 'We aligned on a phased delivery plan that protected engineering capacity.'
Follow-up: What trade-offs did you discuss? 'Revenue timing versus technical debt and hiring plan.'
exec.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for exec. Competency is Conflict Resolution. lowerTranscript.text: Marketing and Product disagreed on launch timing for a new feature. I added it to the weekly exec agenda so leadership could decide.
Did you speak with the other leader first?
I assumed the agenda item would surface the right discussion.
